description: The product vocabulary: every name a user sees and every domain term an implementer uses. vocabulary@<n> is DR-0001@<n>. Generated views: docs/vocabulary.md and frontend/src/vocabulary/labels.ts (node scripts/conformance/run.mjs --write).

positioning.statement: Rounds is a self-hostable career command center that connects a person's canonical professional history and evidence to the opportunities they pursue, the artifacts they submit, the interviews they prepare for, the practice they complete, and the next actions they should take.
positioning.title: Career Command Center

namespaces.description: Stable platform terms. Career packs cannot redefine them (spec 815-840).
Provisional namespace for the Software Engineering pack until #39 takes it over under pack ID software-engineering.

names.name: Audit Entry and Domain Event envelopes

usageRules.rule: "Attempt" labels only Practice Attempt. Execution Attempt and Processing Attempt are inspection-only.
"Profile" alone is never a label. The Profile page is Account; Career Profile is the only profile.
In UI copy, "workspace" means only the Opportunity Workspace.
Account preferences are labeled "Setting"; "Preference" stays with the profile construct.
"Provider" is always qualified: Sign-in provider, AI provider, Calendar provider.
In UI copy, "Capability" means only Share Capability.

values.meaning: The capability remains but its model or interaction changes.
Requires explicit owner approval and a replacement or migration statement.

feature.qualifier: Optional text after the value, such as "and harden" or "without loss".

values.meaning: Preserve as an immutable opaque archive.
Re-enter through a client-assisted reconciliation flow.
Intentionally drop, only after explicit owner approval.

catalogWords.condition: with a time-bounded adapter the transferring leaf owns

cutover.definition: The transformation moves one bounded context at a time. Temporary expand/contract schemas, compatibility adapters, shadow reads, and migration comparison are allowed. Each converted concept has one writable authority, an explicit retirement criterion, and a time-bounded compatibility window. This avoids both permanent dual-writing and one high-risk whole-product cutover.

allowlist.reason: Shipped migration comment for a drop with no data migration. Shipped migrations are never edited.
Shipped migration comment for a drop with no data migration. Shipped migrations are never edited.

terms.definition: Owns authentication identity, security controls, provider connections, product preferences, appearance preferences, locale and accessibility preferences, and data-retention preferences. It does not own professional history or target-opportunity facts; the current Profile page becomes Account.
A product, appearance, locale and accessibility, or data-retention preference owned by Account, including the current campaign selection, which only sets query defaults.
Primary navigation destination for Account identity, security controls, provider connections, and Account preferences, kept separate from professional profile editing.
An external identity provider an Account signs in with, such as an OAuth provider. "Provider" is always qualified.
An AI model provider connection the Account configures. Its credential lives in the account secret store and is used only through the provider gateway. "Provider" is always qualified.
An external calendar service reached through the calendar connector contract. Continuous synchronization is a separate integration workstream. "Provider" is always qualified.

One of the five normative classes (Private, Sensitive, Third-party personal, Secret, Share Projection) that set what may reach remote AI, search, logs and traces, public share, and export, local draft, and backup. A career pack may make a rule stricter but cannot relax it.

Private, the default: profile facts, opportunities, actions, and ordinary practice. Remote AI needs per-request consent after a payload preview; search and index stay inside the owning account; logs and traces carry metadata and opaque IDs only; public share only through a separately reviewed Share Projection; account export, account-namespaced local drafts, and encrypted backup are allowed.

Compensation, immigration, accommodation, private feedback, and protected demographics. Remote AI is off by default with a separate field-level confirmation for one invocation; search is off by default or masked with explicit opt-in; logs and traces carry no field values or reversible identifiers; excluded from public share by default; protected export only, with encrypted local draft and backup.

Recruiter, interviewer, and contact identity, messages, and notes about another person. Remote AI is off by default with purpose-specific confirmation; search stays account-local; logs and traces carry minimized pseudonymous IDs; excluded from public share unless that exact field is intentionally published; included in full account export with a warning, with encrypted local draft and backup.

Provider credentials, reset and session tokens, share bearer material, and encryption keys. Never sent to remote AI, indexed, logged, or shared. Excluded from normal export and browser storage; only an explicit rewrapped secret export; encrypted backup with separate key custody.

Owner-reviewed fields from one immutable Artifact Revision. Never part of remote AI resolution; not added to public indexing; an aggregate view event only when enabled; shared only through its scoped capability; exportable immutable bytes with no browser draft and an encrypted backup of the owner record.

The aggregate root for canonical professional facts. It references typed records rather than storing one undifferentiated document. Profile records support stable identity, revision history, source provenance, confidence when derived, relationships, visibility and privacy classification, and career-pack extensions.
Career Profile construct for how the person is identified professionally: professional name and headline (one per Career Profile).
Career Profile construct for one typed way to reach the person, such as email, phone, or location; one Career Profile has many.
Career Profile construct for an external profile or link, such as a portfolio or public code profile.
Career Profile construct for employment or another engagement the person held; employment and project facts are many Career Profile records.
Career Profile construct for a project or work sample.
Career Profile construct for an achievement or the evidence behind it.
Career Profile construct for a professional narrative or story, including behavioral stories.
Career Profile construct for a skill or competency; packs add profession-specific facets.
Career Profile construct for education or a credential.
Career Profile construct for a publication.
Career Profile construct for a job-search preference or constraint, such as target role, location, or work policy. Account preferences are a different term (Setting).

A proposed fact or relationship: target entity kind, target field or relation, proposed value, create, update, relate, or conflict action, exact source span, source document, confidence, candidate duplicate matches, current canonical value, review decision, and transformation and version metadata.

An immutable record committed before any provider egress: purpose and capability; account, command, source, Processing Attempt, and retry-lineage identifiers; consent, privacy-, retention-, and redaction-policy versions; the exact source-version vector; outbound payload digest; provider endpoint identity, model revision, parameters, prompt-contract version, tool policy, and provider idempotency key; authorization; and intended retention. No network request occurs until the Intent commit succeeds.

An immutable record linked to one Intent, committed after response, failure, cancellation, or reconciliation and before any result is applied: provider request and response identifiers and digests, dispatch, response, and persistence timestamps, succeeded, failed, canceled, or unknown-after-egress state, failure class and token accounting, a Staged Provider Result ID for every success, and final retention.

Logical envelope of an immutable pre-egress Intent and immutable post-egress Outcome for one model attempt. It proves what policy and inputs governed one invocation without retaining sensitive plaintext.

Preserves material submitted for parsing or reference: file or pasted text, source URL and retrieval metadata, media type, checksum, retention and privacy policy, extraction status, parser and model version, and previous processing attempts.

One durable parsing, OCR, URL retrieval, repository analysis, extraction, or reprocessing attempt, in queued, leased, succeeded, failed, canceled, superseded, or stale state, with source checksum, idempotency key, lease, bounded retry, and cancellation.

The privacy-classed, encrypted, retention-bounded normalized result of one successful provider response, linked to one Outcome: versioned extraction or generation payload, source anchors, validation result, response digest, and the deterministic seed that recreates identical claims or proposals without another provider call.

The one capture surface, opened from every page and the Command Center, through which manual entry, natural-language quick capture, paste, files, job-posting URLs, JSON Resume, LinkedIn export, GitHub, and later pack sources feed the common command and ingestion model. Source material is preserved even when extraction fails.
Concurrency token for one mutable record.
Ordered domain state for one aggregate.

One atomic command result that may touch multiple aggregates, identified by account and command ID. Rolling back creates a compensating change set against current expected versions; it never rewinds history blindly.
Named Career Profile change set.
Immutable complete offer terms. Each accepted change to an Offer creates one, containing the complete terms, source, actor, timestamp, deadline, and prior revision.

Immutable record of an authorized mutation: what changed, who or what requested it, authorization context, previous and current versions, and the transaction change set. It is not the user-facing Interview Round or Offer model.
Immutable outbox and integration message emitted after the same transaction commits, with schema version, aggregate sequence, causation ID, correlation ID, account scope, and change-set position.
Revision of an Opportunity's role posting and job description. One Opportunity may have many source revisions; a referenced revision is retained when the Opportunity is archived.
Version of one typed relation, such as Pursuit-to-Campaign membership, which changes only by explicit detach.
Version of an Artifact Edition's wording overrides; removing an override affects future revisions only.
Version of one Account preference, such as the current campaign selection.
Version of a key in the account secret store; revoking it crypto-deletes what it protected.
Version of one Share Capability; revocation and expiry take effect immediately.
Activation and version state of one Pack Activation.
Freshness position of a derived read model, Readiness Snapshot, or search index against its sources.
Version of the algorithm or projector that derived a read model, Readiness Snapshot, Recommendation, or search index.

Represents a company, school, publisher, community, or other organization once. History, education, opportunities, contacts, interviews, publications, and offers reference it. Organization identity permits aliases and merge history.

Represents a recruiter, referrer, interviewer, hiring manager, colleague, or other professional contact once. The relationship to a pursuit or interview event carries the contextual role, rather than one string encoding role and timezone.

Owns the target organization, role or title, canonical job posting, source URL, job description, location and work policy, compensation range when known, extracted requirements, source revision, and archival state. Multiple source documents may contribute to one opportunity.

The continuous workspace for one opportunity. A persistent header shows organization, role, pursuit stage, important date, next action, source state, and campaign lens; sections (Overview, Process, Preparation, Materials, People, Actions, Activity) keep the opportunity context and reference facts rather than copying them. In UI copy, "workspace" means only this.

The user's active or historical relationship with an opportunity. Owns pipeline stage, stage history, dates, disposition, user notes, campaign membership, priority and fit assessment, and relations to people, materials, actions, interview process, and offers. "Application" remains valid user-facing language once a pursuit has been submitted; wishlist and networking stages exist before an application does.

label.specLabel: Application, Opportunity, or Pipeline item according to stage

terms.definition: Owns only the structured hiring-process definition for one Pursuit: optional loops or stages, ordered references to interview Career Activities, default round types and expected signals, default preparation context, and derived progress and outcome summaries. It owns no writable schedule, participant, debrief, outcome, or reschedule history.

The current comparable negotiation aggregate; zero or more per Pursuit. Each accepted change creates an immutable Offer Revision. Offer state and Pursuit state connect through explicit transition rules; one component never silently rewrites another's status.

A user-defined planning goal and time box: name and intent, date range, lifecycle, target criteria, explicit Pursuit membership, optional preparation objective, display preferences, and progress projections. It is a lens over canonical records; interview rounds, Actions, and attempts derive campaign context through their owning Pursuit or an explicit goal relation.

Primary navigation destination for Pursuits: stage-based and list views from one pursuit model, opportunity source health, fit and priority, campaign lenses, saved filters, clear wishlist, networking, and application semantics, and degraded-data indicators. Applications and separate round management become Pipeline and the Opportunity Workspace.

A stateful, user-facing occurrence and the sole mutable authority for its schedule, lifecycle, participants, debrief, outcome, and correction history, such as a scheduled interview round, conversation, follow-up, material submission, milestone, or professional event. Changes go through versioned domain commands, and history is append-only. An Interview Round is a Career Activity kind.

Owns work to be done: title and body, status, due date and optional schedule, priority, effort estimate, recurrence when supported, relations to canonical entities, origin or recommendation reason, and completion effect. Rich-text mentions may render relations, but text does not own relationship identity. Todos become Actions.

A stable recommendation identity derived from an input vector and algorithm version. It can expire or be dismissed, snoozed, or invalidated, and feeds Today and Action creation; it becomes an Action only when accepted.

Primary navigation destination that explains the few actions that matter, why they matter, and what changes when they are completed: a short prioritized narrative queue, not a card index of every subsystem.

Keyboard entry point for universal search, create and capture, navigation, domain commands, recent entities, campaign lens switching, and pending import review. Quick and full forms use the same field definitions and commands.

A purposeful edition such as a resume, cover letter, interview brief, portfolio selection, or future career-pack artifact. Owns artifact type, purpose, target opportunity or audience, selected profile facts, order and grouping, explicit wording overrides, design and template configuration, source profile revision, generated output revisions, submission and freeze state, and export and share history. An edition does not become a second editable career database. Resume Studio and cover-letter generation become Materials.

label.specLabel: Resume, Cover Letter, Interview Brief, or Material

terms.definition: Immutable materialized content and renderer contract: content snapshot, source entity-version map, accepted override values, opportunity revision, template, renderer, font, and asset versions, locale and pagination inputs, byte checksums for retained exports, and creation, submission, and share metadata. A submitted material and a public share always reference one exact Artifact Revision.

AI-authored wording or synthesis, which is not an Extracted Claim. It records task and target artifact, source entity-version map, supporting passages or facts, generated text, model and provider and prompt-contract version, unsupported-claim warnings, reviewer edits, accept or reject decision, and the resulting Artifact Revision when accepted.

A strictly transitional containment bridge: immutable and account-scoped, created only by an authenticated server command after verifying ownership of the current resume, variant, or version, materialized from server-read legacy records and never caller-authored HTML. It stores legacy source IDs and versions, sanitized content, bounded render options, template, font, asset, and renderer versions, and an output checksum or retained bytes; it cannot be edited or treated as canonical career data and is rendered or shared only through the contained worker and capability contracts. ROUNDS-15 migrates each one to an Artifact Revision and retires it once nothing references it.

The trusted, versioned, server-owned contract through which the server materializes markup to render an Artifact Edition, Artifact Revision, or Legacy Artifact Snapshot. The public API never accepts caller-authored HTML, JavaScript, browser flags, filesystem paths, network policy, or renderer commands.

A narrow, unguessable read capability scoped to one immutable Artifact Revision or containment-era Legacy Artifact Snapshot. Only a keyed digest of the bearer token is stored, cleartext bearer material is disclosed once, and expiry, password policy, revocation, and view policy are recorded. It never grants administrative record access, and revocation invalidates it immediately.
Pack-owned practice content keyed (pack, track, slug). A Practice Attempt pins one Practice Item and its career-pack version. AI-coding rounds are Practice Items.
Mutable work in progress on a Practice Item, kept separate from immutable attempts.
An active practice session, such as a running timer, kept as a mutable record separate from immutable attempts.

An immutable result tied to a Practice Item and career-pack version, candidate inputs and durable work artifacts, server-owned harness and test version, execution-environment version, result and evidence, feedback, duration and timestamps, opportunity and campaign context, and causation and correlation identifiers.
One server-side run or evaluation of candidate code under the execution-control protocol and its durable result envelope. It is not a Practice Attempt.

A server-owned, immutable, versioned definition of the tests an execution request is evaluated against. Clients send candidate source and structured input only, never shell commands, executable validators, hidden tests, or expected-result code.
A server-owned, immutable, versioned harness. Any expressive validator runs inside the same isolated worker as candidate code, never through eval in the API or control plane.
A versioned, pack-owned readiness projection with a projection watermark and algorithm version, rebuilt or purged deterministically and read by Today and the preparation plan.

Primary navigation destination for the career-pack practice tracks, Practice Items and Attempts, opportunity context, preparation plans, readiness, history, and feedback. Existing strong practice pages stay recognizable behind the pack contract.

A trusted, reviewed bundle shipped at build time that extends the stable platform core through a versioned manifest: extension schemas, field definitions, validators, relation types, editors and renderers, import aliases, interview-process and round types, practice tracks, attempt schemas, artifact projectors, readiness signals, recommendation contributors, search contributions, migrations, and required capabilities. Packs cannot redefine platform terms.

Account or deployment activation of a pack manifest already shipped with the deployment, atomic across platform contract, schema and handlers, editors and renderers, migrations, projectors, and search contributions. State is inactive, migrating, active, read-only, incompatible, or failed; deactivation keeps pack data read-only.
Software Engineering practice track for system design guides, questions, diagrams, practice canvas, status, drafts, and timers.
Software Engineering practice track for coding lists, the editor, drafts, focus mode, custom runs, evaluation, status, and timers.
Software Engineering practice track for AI-assisted coding files, checkpoints, chat and edit, runner, grade, drafts, and attempts.
Software Engineering practice track for real-world and take-home prompts, files, harness, AI policy, rubric, drafts, and attempts.
Software Engineering practice track for behavioral guides, questions, categories, story links, status, and timers.
